verdicts.note: ESSB 6346 is not the lone taxes evidence: she also voted yes on ESHB 2081 (B&O) and ESSB 5813 (capital gains/estate) in 2025 [S20][S22], voted no on every failed 6346 floor amendment [S18], and her platform asks 'more from those who can afford it' [S5]. Roll calls checked against the cached XML. Her 2024 yes on I-2111 [S24] points the other way but predates three revenue votes, so +2 high stands.

Pole_b record is real (no on I-2113 [S33], treatment/reentry/accountability platform [S5]), but in 2024 she also said she wanted to increase law-enforcement staffing and support so police can focus on violent crime [S17]. That is not 'fully' pole_b; +1.
Direction is right: prior-authorization, charity-care, parity and drug-cost work are fixes within the current system, which is pole_a (negative).
Rests on gender-affirming care, LGBTQIA+ anti-discrimination and abortion-care evidence only [S5][S6]; the I-2081/HB 1296 votes are correctly kept on parental-rights.

Two independent recorded actions: nay on I-2081 (2024, verified in the cached roll call) and named co-sponsor of HB 1296 (verified in the cached House Bill Report) plus yes on both House final-passage votes.

0 means genuinely mixed, but every stated position leans pole_a: no new or higher tax 'without a proven need', examine existing spending before seeking new revenue [S8], 'expanding tax relief' and 'targeted tax relief' for small businesses and families [S6]. The only counterweight is a hedge ('not promising to oppose every tax') and an undefined 'tax equity' phrase, not a pole_b position. Mild restraint, so -1 at medium (campaign statements only, no record).

Direction right, but high overstates it. Every source is his own words (platform [S6], tax-standard release [S8], pamphlet [S1], and his answers in the KDN Q&A [S2]); there is no record. He also pairs audits with new spending pledges ('dedicated funding' for childcare [S6]) and says 'the goal is not simply to spend more or spend less' [S8]. Medium.

Low is the right confidence: one explicit pole_b phrase (growth near transit 'reducing auto dependence and carbon emissions' [S6]) and no CCA position. Puget Sound and shoreline protection is environmental, not climate evidence, and should not raise it.

Never held public office, but he is an elected PCO and 23rd LD state committeeman, sits on the district and county Democratic executive boards, helped redraft the state party platform [S1][S5], and is endorsed by U.S. Rep. Adam Smith [S7]. A party-insider profile is not the maximal outsider case; consistent with the Spokane LD6 treatment of a party officer (+1).
Direction right: insurer accountability, surprise-bill and transparency fixes are explicitly within the current insurance system (pole_a, negative).
